Abandoned OffscreenCanvas pilot, staging, unified-worker, duplicated-runtime, worker-protocol, and worker-bundling paths remain removed. Any future OffscreenCanvas work must move the production renderer rather than recreate it and requires a new explicit parity review.

phase464AReview: The legacy WebGL spike path is extracted into a dedicated WebGL2 runtime with initialization-cached state, one persistent VAO, FFT/sample-rate keyed frequency maps, one authoritative amplitude profile/upload, and two mirrored draws. Auto Zoom eases to neutral without per-frame input or pulse closures, and Orbital Energy uses a bounded normalized Path2D cache instead of per-frame conic gradients. No RAF, timer, worker, canvas, dependency, or recording behavior was added. App.tsx, the Phase 4.5 Core Particle shader, and the 449-line Canvas2D Core Particle fallback remain byte-identical.
phase48AReview: Phase 4.8A introduces a host-neutral VisualizerRenderKernel and MainThreadRenderHost without changing the production executeVisualFramePipeline body. sprintIntegrityLockReview: Sprint 'Integrity Lock' (2026-09-23) intentionally modifies one frozen file, src/app/runtime/visualizer/renderers/CanvasSpikeRingRenderer.ts, to (1) batch the Canvas2D spike-ring stroke submission by resolved color into one Path2D per bucket instead of one beginPath()/stroke() pair per spike, cutting per-frame paint calls from O(N) to O(bucket count) with identical geometry and color output, and (2) replace the fallback Iridize band-recolor with a fresh, additive 'Chroma Flare' pass drawn in its own hue lane past the spike tip and composited with globalCompositeOperation='lighter', so it only ever adds light/alpha on top of the existing spike rather than recoloring or dimming it; the flare is fully gated behind the existing iridize>0.01 threshold and adds zero cost when Iridize is off. The exact production frame body hash (executeVisualFramePipeline) is unchanged, as is App.tsx and the certified Core Particle fallback. No RAF, timer, worker, canvas, or per-frame object allocation was added; Path2D instances are created only per distinct color bucket touched that frame, not per spike. Separately (outside this frozen set), src/app/runtime/visualizer/setup/createRendererViewportSetup.ts had its shouldInitLegacyGL gate changed from `!CORE_PARTICLES_SANDBOX && !useWebGLCoreParticlesRef.current` to `!useWebGLCoreParticlesRef.current`, restoring legacy WebGL spike context creation (and with it GPU Spike Bloom and shader-owned Iridize per phase464AReview) whenever Core Particles isn't actively using the WebGL canvas this session; the frame controller's existing per-frame mutual-exclusivity check (useEngineOwnedGL / legacyWebGLSpikeAllowed) is unchanged and continues to arbitrate between the two GPU consumers at render time.
sprintBReview: Sprint B (2026-09-23, hot-loop performance / Worker BPM / code-splitting) touches one file inside this frozen set: src/app/runtime/visualizer/controls/registerVisualizerControlPlane.ts. The FFT-slider resize handler previously sized spikeFeature.ampBuf/ampEcho1/ampEcho2/tempSmoothingBuf to `audioBuffers.timeArr.length` (analyser.fftSize, the time-domain length) while the frame loop's spike count N is `filteredFreqArr.length` (analyser.frequencyBinCount, exactly half); the two never matched, so the careful linear-interpolation resample this handler performs was discarded one frame later when the frame controller's own `ampBuf.length !== N` mismatch check fired and re-resized with a cruder nearest-neighbor copy. `newLength` now reads `analyser.frequencyBinCount` directly, matching N, so the sizes agree and the redundant second allocation/resample no longer happens on every FFT slider change. No spike geometry, amplitude sampling, or frequency mapping formula was touched. (An IntroTutorial React.lazy()/Suspense code-split in App.tsx was attempted and then reverted in the same sprint, after verify-dist-output.mjs's 'Figma-safe eager UI boundary' check correctly flagged it — that check has no override path in this codebase and its history wasn't visible to us, so App.tsx was restored to its exact pre-sprint static-import form rather than bypassing it; App.tsx is unchanged from the prior sprint.) Neither remaining change touches the exact production frame body (executeVisualFramePipeline, hash unchanged), RAF ownership, or the certified Core Particle fallback.
